question: Atomic radius is usually measured in:
solution:
The correct answer is __**nanometres**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Atomic radius** is defined as the total distance from an atom's **nucleus** to the outermost **orbital** of **electrons**.
 
• Because atoms are incredibly small entities, their dimensions cannot be measured using standard units like **centimetres**, **decimetres**, or **millimetres**, which are meant for macroscopic objects.
 
• The **nanometre** (**nm**) is a unit of length in the **metric system**, equal to **one-billionth** of a metre (**10⁻⁹ m**). It is the standard unit used to express dimensions on an **atomic scale**.
 
• Typical **atomic radii** range from approximately **0.03 nm** to **0.3 nm**. For example, the **hydrogen atom** has a radius of about **0.053 nm**.
 
• The choice of **nanometres** allows scientists to work with manageable **numerical values** when describing the size of **atoms** and **molecules**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Periodic Trends in Atomic Radius**:
 
 
• **Across a Period**: The **atomic radius** generally **decreases** from left to right. This happens because the **effective nuclear charge** increases, pulling the **electron cloud** closer to the **nucleus**.
 
• **Down a Group**: The **atomic radius** **increases** as you move down a column. This is due to the addition of new **principal energy levels** or **electron shells**, which increases the distance between the **nucleus** and the **valence electrons**.
 
 
 
• **Types of Atomic Radii**:
 
 
• **Covalent Radius**: Half the distance between the **nuclei** of two identical atoms joined by a **single covalent bond**.
 
• **Metallic Radius**: Half the distance between the **nuclei** of two adjacent metal atoms in a **metallic lattice**.
 
• **Van der Waals Radius**: Half the distance between the **nuclei** of two non-bonded, isolated atoms in their closest possible approach.
 
 
 
• **Alternative Units**:
 
 
• Another very common unit used for atomic dimensions is the **Angstrom** (**Å**). One **Angstrom** is equal to **10⁻¹⁰ metres** or **0.1 nanometres**.
 
• The **picometre** (**pm**) is also frequently used in modern chemistry, where **1 pm = 10⁻¹² metres**. **1 nanometre** is equal to **1000 picometres**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Scale Comparisons**:
 
 
• **Centimetre**: **10⁻² metres**. Used for everyday objects like **stationery**.
 
• **Millimetre**: **10⁻³ metres**. Used for small mechanical **components**.
 
• **Nanometre**: **10⁻⁹ metres**. Essential for **Nanotechnology** and **Quantum Physics**.
 
 
 
• **Measurement Techniques**: Scientists determine the **atomic radius** using techniques such as **X-ray crystallography** or **electron diffraction**, which provide data on the distance between **atomic nuclei** in various substances.
